papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure. We use this grading to show that Dehn twists give faithful braid group representations in the symplectic mapping class groups of Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds.

papers.title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
papers.abstract: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

papers.title: Lagrangian structures, $r$-matrices and Poisson brackets
papers.abstract: We give a global conceptual viewpoint of two constructions of Poisson structures involving $r$-matrices: the first one concerns coupling of generalized dynamical $r$-matrices with actions of quasi-triangular Lie bialgebras, the second one is given by the mixed products of Poisson spaces, which combine two Poisson actions of a quasi-triangular Lie bialgebra to create a new one. When the input Lie algebroids are integrable, we construct symplectic groupoids for both types of Poisson structures by taking fibred products of Lie groupoid morphisms equipped with shifted lagrangian structures. We illustrate our results with explicit examples coming from Lie theory and moduli spaces of flat bundles over surfaces.

papers.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
papers.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

papers.title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract: A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(\eta,\omega)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $\eta$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $\omega$ satisfying \[ d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega. \] We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families. Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $\alpha$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by \[ \eta=\pi_2^*\xi,\qquad \omega=d(\pi_1^*\alpha)+\pi_1^*\alpha\wedge\eta, \] where $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $\xi$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular, none of these compact homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic structure, even without any invariance assumption. As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.

papers.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,\Omega)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

papers.title: Examples of homological mirror symmetry via Zariski descent
papers.abstract: This paper considers a general setting in which the Fukaya category of an exact symplectic manifold may be decomposed as a fiber product of Fukaya categories of smaller pieces. Following Morimura-Sibilla-Zhou, we expose a property of Fukaya categories that is mirror to Zariski descent of coherent sheaves. The majority of the paper is then spent studying the cases of open Riemann surfaces and exact log Calabi-Yau surfaces, and we provide proofs of homological mirror symmetry in these cases using a local-to-global analysis.

papers.title: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
papers.abstract: Let \(\Sigma_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $\pi_1(\Sigma_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety. Such a symplectic structure fits in the ambient character variety $\chi\big(\pi_1(\Sigma_g),\mathrm{SU}(2)\big)$, where the top stratum of smooth points admits the Narasimhan-Atiyah-Bott-Goldman symplectic structure.
